title: Nuclei Isolation Protocol from Fresh and Frozen Tissue for Single-Nucleus RNA-Seq and ATAC-Seq
author: Zia Hasan

steps.title: Fragment Frozen Tissue
steps.instruction: Fragment frozen tissue into small pieces (roughly rice grain size) using a sterile single-edge blade or surgical scalpel, keeping the tissue on dry ice to prevent thawing and RNA degradation.

substeps.instruction: Use tweezers to hold tissue in place during fragmentation.
Transfer fragmented tissue into a 1.5 mL, 2 mL, or 5 mL microcentrifuge tube.
For tissue weights > 50 mg and up to 100 mg, use a 2- or 5-mL microcentrifuge tube.

steps.title: Initial Tissue Dissociation
steps.instruction: Add chilled Nuclei EZ Lysis Buffer supplemented with RNAse Inhibitor (0.2–1 U/µL) and DTT (1 mM) to the minced tissue.

substeps.instruction: For tissue weight ≤ 50 mg, add 300-500 µL of buffer.
For tissue weight > 50–100 mg, add 500 µL of buffer.
For tissue weight > 100 mg, adjust Lysis Buffer volume accordingly.

steps.title: Homogenize Tissue
steps.instruction: Homogenize the tissue on ice using a pre-chilled plastic pestle by gently pressing down and twisting or lifting against the inner wall of the tube.

substeps.instruction: Keep the tube on ice throughout the process.
Incubate the tube on ice for 5 minutes (1st incubation).

steps.title: Secondary Lysis and Mixing
steps.instruction: Add additional chilled Nuclei EZ Lysis Buffer and mix using wide-bore 1 mL pipette tips (created by cutting the ends of standard tips).

substeps.instruction: For tissue weight > 50 mg and up to 100 mg, add 1000–1500 µL of buffer.
For tissue weight > 100 mg, adjust Lysis Buffer volume accordingly.
Pipette mix 5x; if the tip clogs, continue dissociating with the pestle.

steps.title: Incubate and Optimize Lysis
steps.instruction: Incubate the sample on ice and repeat mixing (5x) using standard 1 mL tips 2-3 times during incubation.

substeps.instruction: Standard incubation time is 5 minutes.
Adjust incubation based on tissue: Olfactory bulb requires 10 minutes; Hippocampus requires 15 minutes.
Perform a lysis timeline (e.g., 10, 15, 20 mins) to optimize for specific tissue types.

steps.title: Filter and Centrifuge Nuclei
steps.instruction: Filter the dissociated tissue through a 70 μm-strainer mesh into a 15 mL or 50 mL Falcon tube (e.g., pluriStrainer Mini).

substeps.instruction: If using a swinging bucket centrifuge, use the 15 mL/50 mL tube.
Otherwise, transfer flow-through to a 1.5 mL-2 mL LoBind tube.
Centrifuge nuclei at 500 x g, 4 °C.
Carefully remove supernatant, leaving approximately 50 µL of the sample.
Remove as much supernatant as possible; leave 50–100 µL if the pellet appears loose.
Vortex DRWB for a few seconds before adding 300–500 µL to the pellet.
Mix gently to avoid creating bubbles.

steps.title: Wash Nuclei
steps.instruction: Wash the nuclei pellet using ice-cold Nuclei Wash and Resuspension Buffer supplemented with 0.2–0.5 U/μL RNase Inhibitor.

substeps.instruction: Remove supernatant using a wide-bore 1 mL pipette tip, then a 200 μL pipette for precise removal.
Add 1 mL of ice-cold Nuclei Wash and Resuspension Buffer (do not pipette mix).
Centrifuge at 500 x g, 4 °C for 5 minutes.
If no visible pellet forms, leave ~200 μL supernatant, add 1 mL buffer, and proceed.

steps.title: Second Nuclei Wash
steps.instruction: Perform a second wash with ice-cold Nuclei Wash and Resuspension Buffer supplemented with 0.2–0.5 U/μL RNase Inhibitor.

substeps.instruction: If pellet is visible, remove as much supernatant as possible; if not visible, leave ~200 μL.
Add 1 mL of buffer and gently pipette mix.
Centrifuge at 500 x g, 4 °C for 5 minutes.

steps.title: Layer Nuclei on DRWB
steps.instruction: Layer the crude nuclei + DRWB suspension onto a fresh layer of DRWB to separate debris.

substeps.instruction: Place 1 mL of DRWB into a new 1.5 mL tube.
Angle the tube and slowly dispense the nuclei suspension along the side wall to create a clear separation.

steps.title: Final Filtration and Resuspension
steps.instruction: Remove the supernatant and resuspend the pellet in 50–500 µL (depending on desired concentration) of ice-cold Nuclei Wash and Resuspension Buffer supplemented with 0.2–0.5 U/μL RNAse Inhibitor.

substeps.instruction: Filter the suspension using a 40-µm Flowmi Cell Strainer (300 µL per strainer).
Transfer filtered nuclei to a new LoBind 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube.

steps.title: Remove Remaining Debris
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the sample to settle the clean nuclei pellet and float the debris.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge at 10,000 x g, 4 °C for 20 minutes (or use a swinging bucket centrifuge at max 4,500 rpm, 4 °C for 20 minutes).
Optional: Pre-rinse 1.5 mL LoBind tubes with 5% BSA solution and dry before starting to prevent nuclei from sticking to walls.

steps.title: Quality Control and Counting
steps.instruction: Assess nuclei quality and count using a fluorescence microscope and hemocytometer.

substeps.instruction: Prepare Nuclei Quality Check and Count Medium.
Vortex nuclei suspension at max speed for 2–3 seconds, then pulse-spin for ≤ 1 second.
Mix 12 μL of the Medium with 12 μL of the nuclei suspension; pipette gently 5–10 times.
Load 10 μL of the mixture into each chamber of a C-Chip Disposable Hemocytometer.
Wait 5–10 seconds for nuclei to settle.
Examine under fluorescence microscope: RFP channel for Ethidium Bromide/Homodimer-1 and Blue channel for DAPI.
Count nuclei in at least two chambers.
